notes.title: Surprise update!
notes.content:
Hey everyone. Long time no talk. Guess what? 

[h1]We have a massive new update for you![/h1]

The most highly anticipated, top-secret, frequently asked-for, totally unanticipated update to Beach Buggy Racing 2: Island Adventure is here! BBR2:IA version 2023.08.08 brings a ton of new content and important tuning updates to the core game as well as improvements to the Hot Wheels DLC and two brand new DLC packs (coming soon).

[h1]Island Adventure Upgrades[/h1]

Top of the list of improvements to the Island Adventure base game is the addition of a new character, Commander Nova. Nova is a canine space explorer with a love of adventure and a passion for liver treats. Her Liftoff ability boosts her forward and above the field of competition, opening up new shortcuts on many of the tracks in the game.

In addition, we have two new city-themed racetracks: Octane City and Sun City Strip. Octane City is a towering car-themed metropolis filled with skyscrapers, with a beautiful autumnal park right in the center. Sun City Strip is a neon-lit beach town with wide boulevards perfect for cruising (and street races). Both city tracks feature our new traffic simulator, populating the roads with cars and taxis to avoid or smash.

We also have the addition of two new cars for your racing pleasure — the pumpkin chariot Screamin’ Jack and the sweet-n-speedy Candy Coupe. 

Finally, we've added a number of a number of additional features and improvements, including car horns and an advanced Photo Mode for taking incredible screenshots. Just hit the Pause button, compose your perfect shot, and hide the UI for a share-ready masterpiece! (Requires gamepad controller.)

[h1]New DLC and Hot Wheels Boosted[/h1]

Oh wait, did I say “finally”? There’s more! Steam users will also have the option of two new DLC: the Turbo Titans Car Pack and the High Octane Moto Pack, as well as free improvements to the Hot Wheels Booster Pack.

The Turbo Titans Car Pack injects a powerful shot of adrenaline with a diverse fleet of five incredible vehicles, including an electric supercar, a wasteland hot rod built from an airplane, and a fire truck themed monster truck. Each machine is crafted with a completely unique persona, designed to refresh your game with a variety of new racing experiences and tactics.

The High Octane Moto Pack lets you experience the roar of engines and the rush of wind against your face with high-speed motorcycle racing. Commandeer three unique bikes: a rugged dirt bike, a turbocharged street beast, and a fusion-powered superbike from the future.

But wait, there’s more! We’re adding brand new content to the Hot Wheels Booster Pack! We’ve got two new cars, the twin-tastic Twinduction and Street Wiener, aka the giant hot dog on wheels. Both cars are available unlocked right out of the box. We’ve also added a new Hot Wheels themed racetrack — the space-themed Outer Limit with upside-down tracks and death defying zero-gravity jumps.

[h1]Full Changelist 2023.08.08[/h1]

[h2]Beach Buggy Racing 2: Island Adventure Update[/h2]
[list]
[*] Two new metropolitan tracks: Octane City and Sun City Strip
[*] Two new cars: Screamin’ Jack and Candy Coupe
[*] New driver: Commander Nova, with Liftoff ability
[*] Photo mode feature from pause menu (requires gamepad)
[*] New spooky theme for Buccaneer Bay
[*] Powerslide tuning & car balancing
[*] Added car horns
[/list]

[h2]Hot Wheels Booster Pack Update[/h2]
[list]
[*] New space themed Outer Limits racetrack
[*] Two new cars: Street Wiener and Twinduction
[/list]

[h2]Turbo Titans Car Pack[/h2] (Coming Soon)
[list]
[*] Javelin: This dragster’s streamlined body and powerful engine make it the epitome of straight-line speed.
[*] X-Stream: A futuristic dune buggy with a flexible open suspension, the X-Stream turns desert dunes into thrilling playgrounds.
[*] Extinguisher: With the Extinguisher monster fire truck, you'll tower over the competition, combining raw power with a heart of service.
[*] Killawatt: A sleek electric supercar that hums with power, the Killawatt embodies pure speed.
[*] Warhawk: Made from the fuselage of an old fighter plane, this rugged three-wheeler thrives in rough terrain.
[/list]

[h2]High Octane Moto Pack[/h2] (Coming Soon)
[list]
[*] Sandstorm: A rugged dirt bike built for off-road dominance. 
[*] Blade 1000R: A turbocharged street beast that's all about speed and precision.

notes.title: Quickie update to fix that controller bug
notes.content:
Ah, the joys of PC game development.  After the last update, we received reports of some players having problems with their controllers.  And of course we haven't been able to reproduce those problems ourselves, which makes fixing a challenge....   

But our best guess  is that in the last update, we included the newest SDL (Simple DirectMedia Layer) controller mapping, to keep things up to date and also add support for PlayStation DUALSHOCK 5 controllers.  Our best guess is that the problem is coming from that.

So this update basically just takes that out and goes back to the old version.  Which means 2 things:
[olist]
[*]If you were having problems with your controller after the last update, please get this one and let us know if the problem goes away.
[*]If, after the last update, you were all "Yay! Beach Buggy Racing 2: Island Adventure recognizes the buttons on my superawesome DUALSHOCK 5 controller!!" .....um, sorry, kid, it's back to generic controller mapping for you.
[/olist]
Anyway let us know if this does (or doesn't! ːsteamsadː) fix your controller problems.  If you had them.  

Thanks!

notes.title: Update: Bug fixin' and Paint swappin'
notes.content:
Hey everyone!  Hope you're enjoying the game so far.  This is our first major update since the game launched.  For the most part we're just fixing bugs and rearchitecting a bunch of stuff under the hood to get ready for a major DLC announcement in the coming weeks.

But don't let that stop you!  This update still has some good improvements, including:
[list]
[*] Physics framerate increased to 120Hz.  Cars should run a little smoother, and fewer collision glitches.
[*] You can now swap and view unlocked car and driver skins in the Collection info popups, and save your preference.
[*] Car painting now triggers from inside the info popups.  So, go to the Collection, open the car you want, and paint from there.
[*] Ghosts are now saved when earning trophies (in Drift, Firework Fury, and Time Trial League Rules) 
[*] Fixed some bugs, including a nasty crash.
[/list]

Enjoy!

notes.title: Release Candidate Incoming!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!  

We just pushed out a new build that fixes a few odds and ends bugs and is officially, we think, we hope, the build which we're going to push to Full Release next week.

That's right, March 10, 2021 is the end of the gestational period of Beach Buggy Racing 2: Island Adventure, and the beginning of...its life?  (I dunno where that metaphor was going.)

Thank you again to everyone who has helped play, test, offer feedback and support to our little cadre of developers while we work on this thing.  It's been fun, and we're not done!  We're still getting tons of feedback to sift through, and we are hard at work on our first major DLC expansion which is going to be REALLY MAJOR.  You'll see.  Just wait a little.

Also, if there's anyone who was thinking of getting the game but was waiting for Early Access to end, here's the choice you're looking at:  
[list]
[*]Wait until March 10 when the game flips over to "full release" and you get to take advantage of a modest launch discount, or...
[*]Get the game now at full price AND grab that special Early Access car and decal gift before it goes away forever on March 10.
[/list]

Either way, you win because fun.

notes.title: Thank you, Early Access players!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

As the days outside grow longer, here in computer land we draw ever closer to the end of Early Access and the beginning of... The Future!  (I wasn't totally sure what to put after the ellipsis... "the First Version"? "the Launch Date"?  all sound kinda dumb.  The Future sounds more awesomer.)

First and foremost, this update contains a special gift for all of you Steam folks who have stuck with us during the [b]Whole Entire Year[/b] that we've been working on this game in Early Access.  Remember a year ago?  When we went to PAX and announced this game and released the first Early Access build, and then the world went to hell in a handbasket and we all just stayed in our houses drinking endless cups of coffee and trying to get Zoom to work?  Ah those were good times.  Um....

Anyway, we really do appreciate all of your feedback and comments and suggestions.  And yes, your money.  You helped our little band of 6 developers push through this challenging year and get this game done.  Sure, we didn't literally change everything that you asked us to change, but we did seriously consider each and every suggestion.  And we did make a [b]ton [/b]of changes and fix a [b]metric ton[/b] of bugs based on your feedback.  And your positive reviews and helpful and supportive comments helped keep us motivated and excited to be working on the game.

And so in thanks we offer you a humble reward.  Wanna be surprised?  Don't read this: [spoiler]It's a new car and an exclusive Steampunk decal.  Get it?  "Steam"punk? The car is more of a sneak peak -- it's for Steam Early Access players only for now, and at some point later in the year we'll release it for other people too.  But the decal is yours.  Only yours.[/spoiler]

In addition to that we fixed a bunch of small bugs and a few notable ones:
[list]
[*] Mr Happy now shows up when you play his cup in split screen.  Thanks [b]frapopap[/b] for finding this one and also:
[*] Time Trial multiplayer results now make actual sense. 
[*] DeatBat doesn't stay sideways when the car that launches it is sideways.
[*] Buncha little bug fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 2020.12.16
notes.content:
Have you ever heard people say the last 10% of the work is 90% of the effort?  Turns out it's kind of true.  We're at the point in development where we are testing, finding bugs, fixing bugs, and grinding some of the rough edges down to a slippery-smooth luster.  

The most significant change in this update is this:  We finally got our translations for French, German, Spanish and Italian integrated!  If you're fluent in these languages, let us know what you think of the translations -- turns out there's no word in German for "Cluck-na-do".

Also you probably noticed we changed our versioning system.  Goodbye, EA-whatever.  Hello, 2020.12.16!  Technically we're still in Early Access but this is the first step of getting everything synced for the final release, and date-based versions is how we're doing it going forward.

Here's just a few of the other fixes and changes:

[*] Changed time scoring criteria to work off rounded 100th's of a second (and an exact match = success)
[*] Added smooth loading fade transitions to server images in Tournaments

[*] Paint screen polish

[*] Fixed sign-in & network check scripting and messaging for Tournaments
[*] Added Narrow font for longer localized languages

[*] Icicle smash count stats now work

notes.title: Version EA-5.2
notes.content:
Folks we are closing in on the end of Early Access.  We can smell it.  The Vector Unit team is feeling that extra burst of energy that comes when you see the light at the end of the tunnel glimmering... although, admittedly, it might be the energy you feel when you think about eating pumpkin pie and gravy and stuff for four days straight.

In any case, we have a pretty sweet update for you.  Not a bunch of fancy-pants, think-they're-better-than you, spectacular big-ticket new features.  Just a little humble polish items here and there, doing their earnest best to make the game better'n'better.

[*] [b]Lots of HUD polish.[/b]  We're now showing the event type, speed/difficulty, trophy criteria, etc. during the pre-game intro cameras, the pause menu, the post-game HUD.  It's pretty neat.  Still need to do that slammin' reward sequence!
[*] [b]UI informational polish.[/b]  That sounds boring, but hopefully you'll appreciate it.  We're just going through the user interface, adding as much info as we can to make the game more intelligible.  Among other things, we added strategy guides for every Powerup.
[*] [b]Lotsa bug fixes. [/b] So many.
[/list]

notes.title: Verison EA-5.0
notes.content:
Folks, this is a big one.  Like, skip Versions 4.7-4.9 big.  It might not seem like much because we've only really got one bullet point, but that bullet's a big one.  It's big because we think Tournaments with leaderboards where we can all finally compete with one another and talk endless smack is a big deal.  But also because this is the last major feature update we have planned before we are done.  ...OK, granted, there's still ton of work to do.  Tuning, polishing, fixing.  All that. But until then, please enjoy:

notes.title: Crickets
notes.content:
Some of you may have noticed that EA-3.8 is missing in action.  We haven't posted an update in 2 weeks, and I'm very sorry to say we're not going to post one this week either.

"WHY IN THE NAME OF ALL THAT IS HOLY AN GOOD?!" you may be yelling, as you roll on the floor clutching your handmade B'Zorp stuffie to your tear-stained vintage BBR1 Powerup T.  Or you might be saying "What's an update?"  Either way, we thought you might want to know what's up.

[h2]EA-3.8 is just too awesome[/h2]
We might have bitten off a little more than we could chew with this one.  

For one thing, we are [b]Going Big with Presets[/b].  You know, those custom rules you can define in Quick Race?  Well we're adding the ability to save custom Presets, so you can hand-craft your very own game mode and then save it out.  You can save a bunch.  And delete them.  Whatever.  We're also working on crafting and tuning some pre-set Presets, just to get you started.

So we also added "[b]Permanent Effects[/b]" to the Preset options.... these are special effects you can apply to the whole race.  Like giving everybody in the race Police Chase for the entire race.  Or Bouncy Tires.  

And then we decided since we did all that we should also put in [b]Handicapping[/b].  Because sometimes you want to play with your Grandma....and your Grandma just smokes you so bad that it's no fun to play with her.  So now you can pick individual handicaps for the better players in your house so the competition stays close and fierce.  

Hmmm... I feel like I'm forgetting something.  Oh RIGHT.  We also added [b]Time-of-Day selection[/b] for Quick Race.  That's something everyone's been asking for.

And that's not even counting a brand new chapter ([b]Wasteland[/b]) on Career, five new [b]gold car skins[/b], two new [b]character skins[/b], and a buncha bug fixes.

Anyway, actually really we are bummed to not have a release for you this week, because we are excited to get this update out to you all.  But we also want to make sure it's ship-shape before we push it through the intertubes, so it's going to take another week.  

Just hug that B'Zorp stuffie a little tighter.  EA-3.8's a-comin'.

notes.content:
With this update we're introducing the first pass of our unlocking system, we've added a swamp-tastic Chapter 5 to Career -- er, "Adventure" -- and we've got 2 new levels for you in quick events.  

[h2]WARNING[/h2]
This build resets everyone's save progress.  We had to reformat the Adventure data, and also introducing the locking system scrambled things up a bit.  Sorry for the inconvenience; this may still happen again during Early Access, but we'll try to firm it up as we get closer to shipping.

[h2]Welcome to the Collection screen[/h2]
Here you can browse the cars and drivers (and more!) you own, and track the criteria that you need to earn the locked ones.  There are a few things you should know about this:
[list][*] [b]Most cars are locked at the start.[/b]  Since we didn't have an unlocking system before, the cars we released previously in EA were unlocked...but now that's all changed.  We're sorry in advance if Twister was your favorite car.  Going forward we'll be adding cars in their locked state, along with Challenges you can complete to unlock them.
[*] [b]Drivers are unlocked at the start (for quick events).[/b]  We want to allow players in quick events to be able to pick any driver right out of the box.  (Well OK there might be a couple of hidden characters who show up later).  But you still need to unlock them in Career mode.  Is this confusing?  Weird?  Awesome?  Perfect?  Please let us know.  
[*] [b]You can unlock special skins -- but not yet.[/b]  Once you've unlocked a car or driver, you'll eventually be able to bring up a new list of Challenges which unlock a special skin for that car or driver.  But this isn't implemented yet.
[*] [b]There will be more.[/b]  So far we've released 22 cars; the final total will be closer to 35.  Also we're trying to add 1-3 more special characters, which will probably be locked or hidden at the start.  And we have other ideas about other collectables -- but more on that another time.
[/list]

notes.title: Major Update EA-2.0
notes.content:

[*] [b]This is a work in Progress!! [/b] That means you [b]may lose save game progress[/b] and unlocks while we are still working on it.  Please just have fun with it, and expect that this'll happen during Early Access.
[*] [b]Drift game added. [/b] Instructions and rules are WIP.  You remember how to drift right?  Tap the brake while turning.
[*] [b]Firework Fury game added.[/b]  Basically a time trial with exploding obstacles.  
[*] [b]Elimination game added. [/b] Instructions and rules are WIP.

notes.title: New Version EA-1.6
notes.content:
A number of big changes and experiments this week:
[list][*] Snazzy new car, the [b]Sand Blaster[/b] is now available for your sand-blasting pleasure.
[*] [b]Full Powerup customization[/b] added for quick events.  You can toggle individual Powerups on/off, as well as whole groups.  Create your own custom game mode like "No Shields" or "Ball ‘n’ Chain Only", or even no Powerups at all!
[*] You can now [b]fire missiles backward[/b]! Hold back on the left analog stick or hold the left shoulder button (L1/LB) to use the look-back camera when you fire, and you can take out a pesky rival behind you. But watch out, the other drivers will be doing the same!
[*] In Championships, you now have the option to “[b]Keep Last Round Powerups[/b]”, and start the next race with an extra edge.
[*] Tweaked some aspects of the [b]Toughness stat[/b] to balance things out and give more importance to tough cars like the Machete, Chomper, or Interloper.
[*] Characters now have individual [b]1st place animations[/b] on Championship podiums (WIP).
[/list]

We've made a number of other important changes to the way Powerups work:
[list][*] Further refinements to the “Balanced Powerups” setting.
[*] Powerup charge timers have been re-tuned to work with the “Balanced Powerups” setting.
[*] Persistent buffs like Shield and Power Vacuum now lock up your Powerup slot so you can’t fill it with another Powerup.
[*] Your own Hazard Powerups such as Jacks, Oil Slick, and Junk in the Trunk can now affect you on the next lap, so drive carefully!
[*] Special Powerup bubble types like Double (two bubbles stacked) and Fast (!) become more frequent as the race progresses.
[/list]

And there are some specific Powerup changes:
[list][*] Hamster Ball and Ball ‘n’ Chain now have a bit of extra oomph.
[*] Power Vacuum no longer lasts until you crash. It has the same duration as the Trampoline.
[*] Cluck-nado Coop now creates its swarm of chickens when an explosion or missile breaks it.
[/list]

As always, this Early Access game is a work in progress and we enthusiastically welcome your feedback.  What do you think of the new customization options?  How do you feel about the tuning changes we've made?  Talk to us in the forums!  We read them every day.
